title: Strict-system projection diamond and its open/proper normalizations
statement: Fix D, l, E, actual strict-system operations o, canonical realization data rho, and a compactified Cartesian square Q [def-sf-completed-projection-exchange-data]. For arbitrary system objects M on X and N on Y, diamondLeft(M,N)=diamondRight(M,N). In addition OpenLaw(M,P_p N) holds and ProperLaw(J_j M,N) holds: the two open restrictions are openSource, and the two proper transposes are commonTranspose. This is an equality in the derived system category before limit, with no input constructibility or Tor condition.

proof.text:
Record the precise compositor/tensor identities used below. Put $C=AU$, $D=U'H$, and write $\mu_C=\mu_A\,A\mu_U$, $\mu_D=\mu_{U'}\,U'\mu_H$, with the tensor factors indicated by evaluation. Monoidality of the canonical open-square compositor is
$$(\sigma_B\otimes\sigma_P)\mu_{A;UB,UP}A(\mu_{U;B,P})=\mu_{U';HB,HP}U'(\mu_{H;B,P})\sigma_{B\otimes P}.$$
For the proper square it is
$$(\theta_B\otimes\theta_P)\mu_{F';GB,GP}F'(\mu_{G;B,P})=\mu_{H;FB,FP}H(\mu_{F;B,P})\theta_{B\otimes P}.$$
These identities are part of the canonical K-flat tensor/composition identifications specified in [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization]. Explicitly, on the simultaneous flat-term K-flat models both routes pull back each factor and balance the same scalar actions; a local pure tensor $m\otimes n$ is sent to its two pulled-back sections in both orders. The structure-ring homomorphisms agree by the two commutative squares, so their scalar multiples agree as well. Thus these are equal chain maps before localization; derived localization preserves the equalities. They apply to the system site itself.

proof.text:
Use [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization] on the simultaneous ringed diagram sites. Write $\beta:HJ\cong J'A$, $\gamma_{j;B,P}:JB\otimes P\cong J(B\otimes UP)$, and set $c=\gamma_{j;K_0,FN}$, $b=\beta_{K_0}$, $c'=\gamma_{j';AK_0,F'GN}$. Thus $c'$ has target $J'(AK_0\otimes U'F'GN)$, retaining the essential $U'$. Put
$$d=(1\otimes\theta_N^{-1})\mu_{H;M,FN},\quad z=J'((1\otimes\sigma_{FN})\mu_{A;K_0,UFN})\beta_{K_0\otimes UFN},\quad v=J'(1\otimes U'\theta_N^{-1})z.$$
Both $vH(c)$ and $c'(b\otimes1)d$ have source $HQ$ and target $J'(AK_0\otimes U'F'GN)$. Their source lies in the essential image of $J'$ by the isomorphisms $H(c)$ and $\beta_{K_0\otimes UFN}$; their target visibly does. Apply $U'$ and the canonical open units. The restrictions of $\beta,\gamma$ become the identity under the comparisons in the cited theorem, and the remaining composites coincide by the explicit identities of step 7, with the common final factor $1\otimes U'\theta_N^{-1}$. Full faithfulness of $J'$ gives
$$vH(c)=c'(b\otimes1)d.$$
This proves the equality in the derived system category, without coefficient evaluation.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] to the proper square on the simultaneous ringed diagram sites of step 6. It applies to arbitrary derived system inputs and needs no geometric separatedness of the schemes. With $e:GS\to S'H$ the proper exchange and $\pi,\pi'$ the counit projections, it gives
$$S'(d)e_QG(\pi_{p;M,N})=\pi_{p';HM,GN}(e_M\otimes1)\mu_{G;SM,N}.$$
For completeness the common transpose is fixed, not just the equality: [def-exchange-projection] gives $\varepsilon'_{HB}F'(e_B)=H(\varepsilon_B)\theta_{SB}$ and $\varepsilon_Q F(\pi_{p;M,N})=(\varepsilon_M\otimes1)\mu_{F;SM,N}$. Thus the transpose of the left side above is $dH(\varepsilon_Q)\theta_{SQ}F'G(\pi_{p;M,N})$. Naturality of $\theta$ moves $\pi$ next to $\varepsilon_Q$; substituting the second formula and naturality of $\mu_H$ reduces this to
$$F'G(SM\otimes N)\cong HFSM\otimes F'GN\xrightarrow{H\varepsilon_M\otimes1}HM\otimes F'GN.$$
The initial isomorphism here is precisely $\theta_{SM\otimes N}$, then $H\mu_F$, then $\mu_H$, then $1\otimes\theta_N^{-1}$. Equality from the cited ringed theorem gives this same transpose for the right side. These are system adjunctions before total inverse limit.

proof.text:
Paste the preceding two equations explicitly. Put $T=J(K_0\otimes UFN)$, so $c:Q\to T$. The definitions [def-exchange-projection], interpreted by [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization], are $\operatorname{PF}^c=S(c)\pi$ and $\operatorname{Ex}_!^c=S'(b)e_M$. Naturality of $e$ at $c$, the open equation of step 8 and then step 9 give
$$\begin{aligned}
S'(v)e_TG(S(c)\pi)&=S'(vH(c))e_QG\pi\\
&=S'(c')S'(b\otimes1)\pi'_{HM,GN}(e_M\otimes1)\mu_G\\
&=S'(c')\pi'_{J'AK_0,GN}(S'(b)e_M\otimes1)\mu_G.
\end{aligned}$$
The last equality is naturality of $\pi'$ at $b$ and tensor bifunctoriality. The first line is the top route, and the last line the bottom route, with $v$ inserting exactly the target pullback/tensor identification. This proves equality of the two actual derived system arrows. Only substitution, naturality and functorial composition were used to paste the factors; no inverse of a projection or proper exchange was taken.

theorem completedProjectionExchangeSystem
    (M : System l E Q.X.obj.left) (N : System l E Q.Y.obj.left) :
    diamondLeft l E o ρ Q M N = diamondRight l E o ρ Q M N ∧
    OpenLaw l E o ρ Q M ((pull l E Q.p.hom.left).obj N) ∧
    ProperLaw l E o ρ Q ((Operations.shriek l E o Q.compactification.i).obj M) N
